Adjust P-values for Multiple Testing

Source: R/significance.R
adjust_pvalues.Rd

Applies a multiple-testing correction to the per-bandwidth p-values of a single result.

adjust_pvalues(result, method = "BH")

Arguments

result

Object of class kernelcomm_result with significance already computed.

method

Character, passed to p.adjust. Note that "BH" and "fdr" are the same procedure under two names.

Value

The same object with p_adjusted populated.

What this does and does not correct

This corrects across the bandwidths of one gene pair. Those tests are strongly positively dependent, because the kernels are nested on the same data and the same permutations, so a Benjamini-Hochberg or Bonferroni correction across them is conservative and not straightforward to interpret. If what you want is a global statement about the curve, prefer sup_p_value from compute_significance, which tests the whole curve directly and needs no correction across bandwidths.

The manuscript applies its FDR threshold across gene pairs, not across bandwidths. To reproduce that, collect one p-value per pair, for example sup_p_value or the value at a chosen bandwidth, and correct across the collection, as with the output of multiScaleAC_batch.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 150
coords <- matrix(runif(2 * n), ncol = 2)
res <- multiScaleAC(coords, rnorm(n), rnorm(n), h = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2), perms = 99)
res <- compute_significance(res)
res <- adjust_pvalues(res, method = "BH")
summary(res)$p_adjusted
#> [1] 0.93 0.93 0.93
